title: Cell Template Bit Output
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet, and choose natural numbers $n,|z|,T,t,r$ and a work-tape index $\tau<k$. Suppose $r<2T+1$ and $t\le T$. Let $e$ be a register state whose input-length and fixed-string-length registers are $n$ and $|z|$, respectively; whose instruction register is the layout index of cell $(t,\tau,r)$; whose preceding-cell register, when $t\ne0$, satisfies $q+\mathrm{stride}=i$; and whose first-instruction register is $t\,\mathrm{stride}$. For a phase $ph$ in the five-element phase set, suppose its nonzero flag agrees with $1\le r$, its phase-$2$ flag agrees with $r=T$, and its not-phase-$4$ flag agrees with $r+1<2T+1$. Then executing the cell template’s operations on $e$ produces exactly the bit string assigned to instruction $i$ by the table construction.
hypotheses_covered: Natural numbers T, t, and r
Work-tape index τ in Fin M.k
Instruction register equals the layout index of cell (t, τ, r)
If t is nonzero, q plus the configuration stride equals i
First-instruction register equals t times the configuration stride
Phase ph is in the five-element phase set
The phase nonzero flag agrees with 1 ≤ r
The phase-2 flag agrees with r = T
The not-phase-4 flag agrees with r + 1 < 2T + 1
